item.title: On the strong Arnold conjecture for Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2611.09694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On several families of flag varieties, we provide examples of degenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms exhibiting significantly smaller numbers of fixed points than predicted by the strong Arnold conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Blakey, Roman Krutowski

item.title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.09034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $\mu \to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.
item.dc:creator: Lei Liu, Pedro A. S. Salom\~ao

item.title: On Lagrangians of Oakley-Usher type
item.description: arXiv:2607.15136v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main theme of this paper is to study symplectic (un-)knottedness of Lagrangian submanifolds which are not tori. Our construction of such Lagrangians is inspired by the generalized Polterovich Lagrangians of Oakley--Usher and relies on an adaptation of symplectic reduction methods going back to Chekanov--Schlenk and McDuff's probes to the case of non-abelian group actions. We compare Oakley--Usher Lagrangians to their (un-)knotted cousins to find that, depending on the situation, they are: (1) not diffeomorphic, (2) diffeomorphic, but not Lagrangian isotopic, (3) Lagrangian isotopic, but not Hamiltonian isotopic, (4) Hamiltonian isotopic. This relationship between them frequently changes when the ambient space is compactified by a symplectic cut. In the companion paper "Lagrangian tori in the three-dimensional quadric and mirror symmetry", we focus on monotone tori in the three-dimensional quadric and compute their enumerative invariants and study their relationship to mirror symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Jo\'e Brendel, Andrea Piccirilli

item.title: Contact Surgery Numbers of the 3-torus
item.description: arXiv:2607.25772v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study contact surgery numbers for contact structures on the 3-torus. We show that all contact structures obtained via contact surgery along a Legendrian Borromean ring are overtwisted, and that this construction yields infinitely many pairwise non-contactomorphic contact structures on $\mathbb{T}^3$. We prove an obstruction on the maximal Thurston-Bennequin invariant of 3-component links to produce $\mathbb{T}^3$ by Dehn surgery. We also compare Legendrian surgery presentations of the Stein-fillable contact structure on $\mathbb{T}^3$. In this setting, we exhibit a non-destabilizable Legendrian knot with no graded normal ruling whose associated Stein filling has nonzero full symplectic homology.
item.dc:creator: Prerak Deep, Monika Yadav
